guardrails: GCMS reference matching is pattern guidance, not formula reconstruction.
Use matches to inform original Beach Box design decisions and controlled testing.
Do not copy commercial formulas, exact GCMS percentages, or reference material breadth.
This report does not change active formulas, IFRA logic, pricing, accord recipes, sensory data, candidate statuses, UI, or AI behavior.

formulas.referenceResemblance: Most references overlap through Airy Diffusion Architecture, Skin Musk / Soft Base Architecture, Woody Amber / Driftwood Architecture.
formulas.beachBoxDivergence: Uses proven modern woody/musk diffusion as a frame, then bends it toward salted skin, mineral air, and driftwood.
formulas.whatThisSuggests: Treat the GCMS corpus as evidence for construction roles, then test the Beach Box formula on skin before changing dosage or materials.
formulas.whatNotToCopy: Do not copy exact GCMS percentages, commercial material breadth, or reference-style citrus/musk bulk blindly.
formulas.potentialUsefulMove: Validate whether the marine/mineral heart feels skinlike and coastal before adding more marine force.
formulas.riskCaveat: Marine/mineral materials can become loud, metallic, or generic before they become more realistic.

worthConsideringLater.reason: Worth reviewing later for skin-warmed floral body if wear tests need more humid heart volume.
Only consider if drydown needs warmth; avoid if it turns the coastal skin direction gourmand.
Only useful as citrus lift if the opening needs sparkle; citrus oils may already cover part of this role.

topReferenceMatches.keyDifference: The overlap is mostly woody/musk structure; Beach Box keeps the coastal skin and mineral story as the differentiator.
topReferenceMatches.usefulLesson: Use this as evidence that airy woody amber plus transparent floral/musk lift can carry trail without adding more aquatic force.

crossFormulaLessons.topic: Best embodiment of proven modern construction patterns
crossFormulaLessons.lesson: This formula has the densest overlap with recurring airy diffusion, woody amber, musk, and transparency patterns; use wear tests to decide whether that strength feels like Beach Box rather than generic modern structure.
Lower direct reference resemblance can be valuable if the Beach Box coastal skin/marine/wood idea reads clearly in wear tests.

crossFormulaLessons.topic: Highest risk of overusing marine/mineral effects
crossFormulaLessons.lesson: Treat marine/mineral overlap as a restraint signal: test realism and skin integration before increasing Calone/Oceanol/seaweed-style force.
The woody/musk base is the most commercially familiar architecture; use it as support, not as the whole identity.
The model can compare construction patterns, but skin evolution, projection, and drydown appeal remain unproven without controlled testing.
